question: to the Commission Peter Agius (PPE) Subject:

Industry reports indicate that in the coming weeks, certain flights around Europe may be disrupted due to a shortage in the supply of jet fuel. In this situation, EU Member States will need to use their own stockpiles of jet fuel. However, the new anti-tankering measures in the ReFuelEU Aviation Regulation1 oblige uplift 90 % of their required fuel at the departure airport. While Malta has a sufficient local supply of jet fuel, the anti-tankering rules will make the island’s connectivity dependent on fuel supplies in European hubs. In view of this: 1.
What immediate measures is the Commission taking to assess and mitigate the risk of flight disruptions in the EU caused by jet fuel shortages?
What implementing powers under the ReFuelEU Aviation Regulation could the Commission use to safeguard island connectivity in cases of shortages and emergencies?
Is the Commission ready to suspend anti-tankering rules temporarily to safeguard island connectivity, in particular air connectivity?
https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/2405/oj.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.7.2026) 1. To strengthen preparedness, and as announced in the AccelerateEU Communication1, the Commission has established a Fuel Observatory to monitor EU production, imports, exports and fuel stocks. This improves visibility over supply and demand, helps detect shortages, and supports targeted action, such as alternative sourcing or coordinated stock releases in the EU. Given the context, the Oil Coordination Group meets more often to review EU oil supply security and coordinate action as needed2. The Commission also issued on 8 May 2026 guidance on the flexibilities available under EU aviation legislation to ensure coordination across Member States3. This covers airport slots4, travellers and passenger rights5, fuel uplift obligations under ReFuelEU Aviation6, Public Service Obligations (PSOs)7, and the use of alternative jet fuel sources. 2 and 3. The Commission recognises the specific challenges faced by islands, where air connectivity is essential. The AccelerateEU Communication sets out measures to preserve the functioning of the Single Market while safeguarding essential air connectivity across the EU, including island regions. Regarding the ReFuelEU Aviation Regulation, the guidance on the flexibilities clarifies how airlines can uplift more aviation fuel at the departing airport for compliance with fuel safety rules under Article 5(2). Airports located in outermost regions are not considered within the Regulation. Finally, at present, there is no immediate threat to the security of supply, although stocks of some fuels are tight. If the situation worsens and the existing flexibilities no longer suffice, the Commission will propose temporary changes to the legislation, where justified.
